**Independent review of A1 design r6 round 4 (delta review) at `2aec244e283fc49a85af04f2d9c3a72ec4122340`: reviewer text, verbatim.**

Reviewer: a Claude reviewer agent started with a fresh context, given only the review request and the commit; it wrote none of the reviewed work and made no GitHub or repository writes (owner decision at #1169 comment 7166418469). Redaction: no redaction. SHA-256 of the unredacted review text: `594dc1e79b26868951b1157185d17116a00fad8f87cec247b4bda691bb8720c7`. Writer responses, if any, are posted separately; acceptance is the owner's decision.

---- reviewer text begins ----

## Delta review: A1 design r6 round 4 (2aec244e283fc49a85af04f2d9c3a72ec4122340 vs c33d5b71a3e4e15028d19ff153afcee8f5aa90a3)

**Verdict: ACCEPT WITH NITS.** I found no genuine error that needs another cycle. The nits below can go into the adoption record or the tool revision.

### How I checked
- Read-only throughout. I made only `gh api` GETs and wrote nothing to git or GitHub.
- I read the full diff of the r6 directory (14 files) and #1169 comments 7169906297 and 7169923380.
- **Reproduction (check 5).** I followed the manifest recipe (LANDING-MANIFEST.md:42) in a scratch layout: `out-final4/` holds the c33d5b71 files with generator-round3 as `build/` and its inputs; `c33/` is the c33d5b71 directory; `out-final5/build/` holds correct4.py and its four inputs.
  - `python3 -I -B correct4.py` exits 0 and its self-rerun passes.
  - All 12 outputs are byte-identical to 2aec244e, including LANDING-MANIFEST.md (3ae6b8b2…) and CORRECTION-REPORT-round4.md (5f865f8c…).
- **Inputs.**
  - `records-1169.json` matches both live comments in body, created_at and login.
  - `review-r6-round3.md` equals the text between the reviewer markers of 7169923380, stripped, with sha256 05b42b1c… as that comment states.
  - Every decision line in `owner-decisions-A1-A5.json` occurs verbatim, sentence by sentence, in 7169906297.

### Check 1: the diff matches the authorized scope
- **EXPECTATIONS.json.** Only TR45, TR45-opB, TR45-opC and item11-T1p change, plus `record_id`. The other 554 rows and `retired` are byte-identical.
  - The three TR45 rows change only `not_run`, `flags` and, for TR45-opB, `status_allowed`, which now admits NOT RUN. `expect` and `restored` are unchanged.
  - item11-T1p changes only its two flags (A2).
- **REQUIREMENTS.json.** The 428 ids are unchanged, in the same order, and no `controls` list changes. Only two fields change:
  - `owner_decision`, on 56 requirements: 53 for A4, plus R6.STAT.8 (A3), R6.OUT.15 and OBL-17 (A1).
  - `pending_owner_confirmation`, on 50 requirements, now cleared.
- **R6.TREE.12 and LC-7** (DESIGN-r6.md:4089, Table 17.1). The condition now reads "until LC-7's cases are restated by an owner-approved expectation change", as the round-3 review recommended.
- **R6.TREE.19.** All three round-3 clarifications are applied:
  - (a) the program is a generator; a class that names none stays REVIEW_REQUIRED;
  - (b) the isolation of R6.DELEG.3, with this requirement's own failure classes;
  - (c) a generator that is not byte-deterministic yields a fail-closed FAIL.
- The other changed files (AUTHORIZATIONS.md, PARAPHRASED-DECISIONS.md, FRESH-AUTHORIZATION.md) carry only the consequences of A1–A5. I found nothing beyond scope.

### Check 2: no retirement gate depends on a deferred row
- **OBL-17** (DESIGN-r6.md:5391, table row 5188) now gates "none while deferred".
- **C-4 of OBL-28** (DESIGN-r6.md:5515) no longer lists TR45-opC as a row without a runner.
- **R6.GATE.9, R6.GATE.15, R6.CTRL.5 and R6.CTRL.17** consistently record TR45-opB and TR45-opC as NOT RUN with the deferral as reason. The composite TR45 is NOT RUN by inheritance.
- **The release check is a constant false**, so the NOT RUN can never become `status-not-allowed`.
- **The NOT RUN form cannot make a non-deferred check pass vacuously.**
  - The rows that admit NOT RUN are the same as before, plus TR45-opB.
  - Every other row keeps its `status_allowed`.
  - The requirements that also name TR45-opB (R6.REC.16, R6.REC.24, R6.CFG.8, R6.CTRL.23) all have other controls, and TR45-opB tests only the deferred replay.
  - No mutant depends on TR45-opB alone. The five MUT rows that list it as a killer have 13 or more other killers in an informational field.
  - No `depends_on` names a TR45 row.

### Check 3: A3 wording and A4 scope
- **A3.** Every sentence quoted at DESIGN-r6.md:185 and AUTHORIZATIONS.md:198 occurs verbatim in 7169906297. R6.STAT.8 is satisfied.
- **A4.** 53 = the 50 requirements found under S1-D3 + R6.OUT.5, R6.OUT.18 and R6.DELEG.8 (round-3 F3). This is exactly the set marked in REQUIREMENTS.json and the design. Each carries "within the reviewed r6 scope and subject to previously approved deferrals", and the decision says it does not extend to unidentified requirements. No "Pending owner confirmation" marker remains.

### Check 4: LANDING-MANIFEST.md
- **Commit reachability.** I tested every one of the 80 40-character ids against main 4c3ad079.
  - The 18 commits marked "on main" are ancestors of main.
  - The 7 commits marked "on main once the landing merge keeps the branch history" are on the branch and not on main.
  - The 6 commits marked "not on main" are on neither.
  - Spot-checks with `gh api compare`: a3799244 diverged (ahead 3), c33d5b71 diverged (ahead 7), 0adc410c behind (an ancestor of main).
- **Blob reachability.** Checked by object walk:
  - the 2 marked "on main" are on main;
  - the 37 marked "once landed" are only on the branch;
  - the 9 marked "not on main" are on neither.
- **Comments.** Every comment classified "support on main" has its body in a landed snapshot (generator-round2 `comments-1169.json`, generator-round3 `comments-round3.json` or generator-round4 `records-1169.json`).
- **Support off main in sec. 4.** The items listed are correctly identified and complete.
  - The 12 requirements resting on edits_check.py match the design's own adoption trace (DESIGN-r6.md:5211).
  - A corpus scan for references to `P` turns up only items already classified elsewhere:
    - R6.GATE.7 and R6.GATE.8, the external oracle, are certification evidence;
    - the control rows in Table 17.1 (part of R6.CTRL.30) are covered by sec. 4's third bullet;
    - R6.EVID.5 is a scope statement;
    - OBL-14 states that it does not depend on `P`.
  - The statements about tool commit a3799244, CI run 45569710442 and `T1'` match the design's sec. 32 row, which lists them.
  - The manifest correctly says that edits_check.py needs an owner decision, since A5 does not cover the blob.

### Findings (all nits, none blocking)
1. **TR45-opC has no runner, yet the text says "the runner records them NOT RUN".**
   - Where: DESIGN-r6.md:2853 (R6.GATE.15) and :5515 (C-4); EXPECTATIONS.json, row TR45-opC, has `runner: null`.
   - Evidence: R6.GATE.2 says a row whose runner is null is reported missing (`missing-id`). Some trivial runner that records NOT RUN is still needed. Similarly, TR45-opB's existing runner (conformance_controls.py:2263) must record NOT RUN rather than run the replay.
   - Impact: this fails closed. Nothing depends on the replay itself, only on a stub that records NOT RUN.
   - Fix: in C-4, add "TR45-opC: a runner that records NOT RUN with the deferral reason". Or leave it to the tool revision.
2. **The A3 quotation joins five of the record's paragraphs into one.**
   - Where: DESIGN-r6.md:185.
   - Evidence: "byte-exact as relayed" is true against the relay file, and every sentence is verbatim against the record.
   - Fix: optional. Say "verbatim sentence by sentence", or keep the paragraph breaks.
3. **The manifest lists three comment ids that do not exist.**
   - Where: LANDING-MANIFEST.md:317–319, ids 7393184198, 7416978004 and 7428102037.
   - Evidence: these digit runs are substrings of blob 318fe33d…, commit 4e9a1501… and sha256 834a1ce2…, so they are false matches by the scanner.
   - Impact: harmless, since they are classified as provenance.
   - Fix: drop the three rows.
4. **The note that correct4.py carries only the listed references is slightly wrong.**
   - Where: LANDING-MANIFEST.md:71.
   - Evidence: correct4.py:677–681 also names 3184c7f9…, 4d864dbd… and blob 6b1280fa…, which are not in the table. All three are reachable from main, so there is no gap.
5. **One id is classified as a reference when it is a computed value.**
   - Where: LANDING-MANIFEST.md:117, 86d79863….
   - Evidence: this is an expected blob id computed from content on main, not a reference to content off main. "Provenance" is harmless, but "not a reference" is more accurate.
6. **generator-round4 lands, although A5 names only the round-2 and round-3 generators.**
   - The manifest flags this explicitly for the owner's merge decision. That is the correct handling, and I raise it only so the owner sees it at merge.

### Limitations
- I did not re-review the parts of the design that round 4 left unchanged, run the tool, or run any control.
- The completeness check of the manifest's references is a regex scan for 40- and 64-character ids, comment ids, #numbers and 11-digit run ids, run against the files that land.
- This review was run by a Claude agent from the same model family as the writer. It is non-author only in that it wrote none of the reviewed work.

---- reviewer text ends ----
